newsitem.title: USA: Virgin's Branson sees BA/American alliance stopped.
newsitem.headline: Virgin's Branson sees BA/American alliance stopped.

text.p: Virgin Atlantic President Richard Branson said on Tuesday he was confident that antitrust bodies would ultimately prevent the proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines.
But he said that if the alliance did go ahead, then the world's other major airlines would consider forming a rival alliance.
Branson was speaking on CNN's Moneyline program, the day before he and other airline executives were to testify at a Congressional hearing on airline regulation.
"I think that public opinion is beginning to move quite strongly against British Airways and American Airlines getting together," Branson said.
"So we're beginning to become more and more hopeful that we can see it stopped," he added.

If the alliance went ahead, he said it would force the other major airlines in the world to get together. And if regulators allowed the BA/American alliance to proceed, they would have to allow others to do the same, he said.
"I'm sure that United, Virgin, Continental, Delta, all the rest of us will sit down and decide to get together as well," he said. "And the Department of Transportation could not stop us.

"Ultimately, that is not in the consumers' interest, and what we're trying to do is get Congress to realize and get the Department of Tranpsort(ation) to realize that it's much better that they tell the two biggest airlines in the world to get on and compete," he added.

Asked about a compromise suggestion that BA and American should give up slots for flights to the United States from London's Heathrow airport, Branson said: "It would have to be an awful lot of slots."
Branson also said that the health of the global airline market was generally very good.

"You've got fuel prices coming down, you've got very high load factors. There's been a slight hiccup in America over the last three months, but I think you'll find (the U.S. market is) going to have a very buoyant summer," he said.
